title: Semisimple group schemes and their scheme-theoretic derived series
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field] [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Use $F$-group schemes and their homomorphisms [def-sc-group-scheme], closed and normal subgroup schemes [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup], smooth morphisms [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], connected schemes [def-weil-connected-scheme], finite-type morphisms [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and affine schemes [def-pc-scheme]. For any $F$-group scheme $G$, let $c_G:G\times_FG\to G$ be the commutator morphism $(x,y)\mapsto xyx^{-1}y^{-1}$. An inclusion $i:D\to G$ is a derived subgroup inclusion if it is a closed subgroup, $c_G$ factors through $i$, and for every closed subgroup $j:K\to G$ through which $c_G$ factors there is a morphism $f:D\to K$ with $j\circ f=i$. Define recursively that $G$ has derived length at most zero if it is the trivial group scheme (its underlying $F$-scheme is terminal), and has derived length at most $n+1$ if it has a derived subgroup inclusion $D\to G$ with $D$ of derived length at most $n$. Call $G$ solvable if it has finite derived length. Call $G$ semisimple if it is smooth, connected, affine and of finite type over $F$, and every smooth connected solvable normal closed subgroup scheme is trivial.
